history.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: revised reusable ARC Daily Digest evening editorial scene, wide landscape. Input image 1 is the edit target: keep the snowy-city composition, enormous friendly bunnies, fantastical GPU tower, the EXACTLY FIVE separate fluffy black spider mascots and golden winter light. Input image 2 is Chen's actual full-size owner-supplied bunny photograph, authoritative for coat markings and ear anatomy. Input image 3 is our clean two-bunny character reference derived from that photo. Input image 4 is our clean Dries Smit character reference derived from his own Hall of Fame card. Make these specific changes: (1) Correct the two enormous bunnies to match images 2 and 3. Keep the foreground bunny grey-brown, with BOTH floppy lop ears hanging down beside its cheeks; its ears must never stand upright. Keep the larger bunny behind it dark charcoal-brown and white, with tall dark upright ears, broad irregular white forehead-and-nose blaze, white cheeks and chest and dark mask around the eyes. Both remain colossal relative to the buildings. (2) Add ONE clearly visible human-scale Dries Smit on the right side beside the GPU tower, wearing the recognizable dark cyber-engineer suit, cyan/green accents, swept brown hair and small green-grid right-eye eyepiece from image 4. He is enthusiastically helping one of the existing spiders install a graphics card into the tower; make the collaboration clear, with his hands touching the card and the spider helping from below or beside him. He must be a small human beside the tower, vastly smaller than the bunnies, visible and recognizable rather than hidden among the cables. Keep all FIVE existing spiders visible and countable; Dries is an additional human, not a sixth spider. No other humans. Do not remove a spider to make room. Friendly cooperative sporting humor, no violence or humiliation. Preserve the painterly cinematic 3D scene style, snow, ruins, warm expressive faces and the absurd fan-cooled graphics-card machine. Clean image only: no words, letters, labels, logos, ranks, scores, watermark or score panel. The score panel will be drawn separately from fresh evidence. The suit, spiders and GPU machine are editorial metaphor, not literal hardware or roster headcount.
